title: Rack your cups in a drying rack another robot arm is also filling
instruction: Put the two green cups from the green mat into the drying rack, one cup to a bay.
context: Two people washing up share one drying rack: each takes a free slot, and waits while the other is putting something in. This checks that a policy can use a rack with just enough room for both, beside a second arm that is filling it too and cannot be talked to.
setup: A 90 x 90 cm wooden table top, 75 cm high. Two YAM arms stand side by side at the back edge, 50 cm apart; the controlled arm is the right one in the screenshot. Distances are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward, and sideways toward the controlled arm. A white drying rack on the centre line, centred 31 cm forward: one row of four square bays running away from the arms, each 5 x 5 cm inside with 5 cm walls, about 22 cm long in all. A green 20 x 20 cm mat 30 cm forward and 27 cm toward the controlled arm, with two green cups (3.4 cm across, 3 cm tall, 70 g) standing on it 10 cm apart; a blue mat and two blue cups the same toward the other arm. The other arm puts its blue cups into free bays, keeping its hand away from the rack while the controlled arm's hand is there. It does the same in every trial.
scoring: The share of the two green cups that are down in a bay of the rack at the end (inside the rack, the cup's middle below 70% of the wall height; standing or leaning). A bay fits one cup. 0 if the two arms ever touch; the run stops at the first touch, and 1 s after both cups are in.
reset_notes: Take all four cups out of the rack and stand them back on their mats, as in the screenshot.
fidelity: Approximate. The cups are solid cylinders, not hollow. Arm links collide as fitted capsules slightly larger than the real ones, so a near miss under about 1 cm can count as a touch. The gripper pinches with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains, gravity compensation and motor torque-speed limits. The other arm is scripted on the true scene state.
